question: Should OpenClaw establish this dedicated AI-safety taxonomy and plugin permission contract in core, or extend the existing diagnostic/security event pipeline and keep detector-specific policy in plugins?
rationale: The answer determines the permanent public Plugin SDK, trust boundary, event ownership, storage lifecycle, and exporter contract; mechanically repairing the current branch would prematurely choose those product and security semantics.

options.title: Extend canonical diagnostics
options.body: Add approved safety event variants to the existing host-owned diagnostic pipeline and inject an identity-bound plugin emitter through the loaded runtime context.

options.title: Approve a dedicated channel
options.body: Keep a separate dispatcher only with explicit lifecycle, queueing, persistence, exporter, protocol, and plugin-identity contracts equivalent to the canonical diagnostics path.

options.title: Narrow or pause the feature
options.body: Land no new public contract until a smaller taxonomy-only design is sponsored, leaving dashboards and detector integrations to later plugin work.

recommendation.title: Extend canonical diagnostics
recommendation.body: Add approved safety event variants to the existing host-owned diagnostic pipeline and inject an identity-bound plugin emitter through the loaded runtime context.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core product scope and a security-sensitive public plugin contract, and recent history connects this person to both plugin policy and product review.
